recentItems.title: Gavin Lynch: 25 Years Of Betting | On The Wire On The Road
recentItems.description:
Andrew Blair White is on the road for a new three-part series around Irish racing, and he begins in Dublin with Gavin Lynch.

Gavin has been betting for twenty-five years, and three years ago he stopped doing it on the flat altogether. He explains why, what giving up Dundalk taught him first, and why arriving fresh in October beats grinding through a summer.

He talks about his father, a small trainer who ran a horse into third in the Triumph Hurdle and took him racing every Saturday from the age of six. About the year he spent as a bookmaker after coming home from Australia, standing up at Thurles waiting for someone to whisper him a winner that never came. 

Gavin explains why the worst opinion you can have is half an opinion, why every punter should keep a P&L, why specialising beats spreading yourself across five sports. He also looks back on five years of Upping The Ante with David Jennings, and talks about the members' service he runs now from November to March.

Then off to Bellewstown, celebrating 300 years of racing, where Gavin has three hours of form study behind him and €300 to play with and all of it going to the Curragh to Curragh Charity Cycle.

recentItems.title: Big-priced Acclamation Star takes Group 3 honours at Salisbury | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Acclamation Star produced a career-best performance to gamely land the IRE-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Dick Poole Fillies’ Stakes at Salisbury.

Without a victory since winning at Bath on debut, James Owen’s juvenile was a 28-1 shot in the hands of Kieran Shoemark, who had no hesitation in striding on aboard the daughter of Acclamation.

Richard Hannon’s Dark Issue and Kevin Philippart De Foy’s Sweet Solera Stakes runner-up Nuit d’Eclair came to challenge inside the closing stages, but they had to settle for second and third place respectively as Acclamation Star proved too tough to pass, registering a half-length success.

Owen told Racing TV: “She hit the gates really well and the plan was to take a handy sit. She perhaps over raced a little bit early on, but as soon as she got daylight she settled lovely and Kieran rides great and knows this track better than we do. She toughed it out really well.

“I think these tactics will be used again in the future. She gets six furlongs and could go seven looking at her pedigree.

“It’s lovely to have a winner for the owner-breeder Peter Gleeson. When I was pre-training he was my landlord at my stables, which I rented off him before I managed to buy them. It’s lovely to repay him with a Group winner.

“She’s pretty smart and I always thought she would nick a bit of black type. The plan after this was to go to the Listed race at Newmarket. Whether we go there now with a penalty or look to go somewhere else, I’m not sure.

“She has a bit of size and scope and will train on next year as well, so there is no rush.”

recentItems.title: King George Hero Banbridge Wins on the Flat at Gowran | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
King George VI Chase-winner Banbridge (4/1) proved a surprise star turn on the Flat at Gowran Park in September 2026, merrily landing the concluding Racing Again September 19th Maiden on his first start on the Flat at the age of 10.

Winner of both the Punchestown Champion Chase and King George in 2024, Banbridge had previously unseated rider in April's Grand National, and was using today's reappearance as a prep run for the American Grand National at Far Hills on October 17.

Racing behind the leaders, strong-travelling Bandridge swept aside his rivals over a furlong out and was an eased-down winner under jockey Joey Sheridan, beating Ballybawn Belter by two lengths.

Regarding the Ronnie Bartlett-owned gelding, winning trainer Joseph O'Brien, earlier successful with the Sheridan-partnered Starborn Legend , said “We didn't expect him to win, but thought it'd be a nice place for him to get the season off to a start. He really went through the race with great enthusiasm and he won snug.

Zavateri won the Celebration Mile at Goodwood, Alfred Wallace took a Solario the data doesn't rate highly, and Light Of Dawn came out on top of a race full of trouble in running, with Eabha arguably the unlucky one.

recentItems.title: MAGNY COURS strikes at Group 3 level for Daniel McLoughlin | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Magny Cours booked her ticket for the Prix de la Foret at the Arc de Triomphe meeting at ParisLongchamp after running out an impressive winner of the Coolmore Stud Little Big Bear Stakes at Cork.

Daniel McLoughlin’s three-year-old filly had contested the Irish 1,000 Guineas at the Curragh in May after finishing runner-up to True Love in a trial at Leopardstown in April only to run too keen and finish down the field.

But returned to seven furlongs, she was sent off 9/1 under Ben Coen before routing a decent line-up by two-and-a-half lengths to tee up a return to the top table at ParisLongchamp on the first Sunday in October.

“On her run in Leopardstown she showed what she’s capable of, especially when she’s able to get her toe in,” said McLoughlin. “It’s brilliant when a plan works out. It’s been a long wait on the weather. I was hoping that it would be worth it and it was, it was more than worth it."

recentItems.title: Group Three honours for Light Of Dawn, James Doyle, Karl Burke and Wathnan Racing! #horseracing
LIGHT OF DAWN lands 2026 Prestige Fillies' Stakes at Goodwood for re-routed James Doyle | Full Race
recentItems.description:
James Doyle may have missed a Group winner in France when his flight to Deauville failed to take off but he parachuted in to Goodwood to pick up a valuable consolation prize in the 2026 Virgin Bet Prestige Fillies’ Stakes aboard Light Of Dawn.

Wathnan’s retained jockey had been due to fly to Normandy to partner Hamad Al Jehani’s Diego Ventura, winner of the Group Three Barriere Prix Quincey, only to be grounded at Duxford Airfield.

But after rerouting to the Sussex Downs, Doyle replaced Clifford Lee on the Showcasing filly and powered to a convincing success, landing the Group Three prize on the 4-1 shot by a length and a quarter from Eabha with the John and Thady Gosden-trained Baaeed filly Coaxed back in third.

“We got to the plane to go to Deauville but that didn’t take off but the plane to Goodwood was there so I switched over and I was quite lucky in that regard,” Doyle told Racing TV. “Obviously I’m delighted to get on her and I was very pleased with her."

#horseracing #goodwood

recentItems.title: JM Jungle toughs it out to take the 2026 Beverley Bullet | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Jm Jungle got up in the dying strides to claim the 2026 William Hill Beverley Bullet Sprint.

A Group Two winner last season and sent off the 7-4 favourite, class told in a thrilling finish on the Westwood as the six-year-old finally got his nose in front after giving a good account of himself in high-ranking contests once again this season.

The John and Sean Quinn-trained gelding was only beaten two and three-quarter lengths in the Nunthorpe at York last week and quickly returned to action got a deserved first victory of the season in East Yorkshire.

Five of the eight runners were still in with a chance as they entered the final furlong with Tim Easterby’s Argentine Tango holding the advantage on the rail as they entered the last 100 yards and Jm Jungle pursuing down the centre of the course.

Jm Jungle responded to the urgings of regular pilot Jason Hart, reeling in Argentine Tango before asserting close home to register a half length success. Badri was a neck further adrift in third and course specialist Elegant Erin a short head off that rival in fourth.

John Quinn said: “He’s done that really well and he’s been running really well all year in Group Ones so he deserved it.

“He ran well in the Nunthorpe, he ran well at Royal Ascot, he ran well at Goodwood and he just got his head in front today.

“He’s in the Flying Five at the Curragh in two weeks so he might go there.”
